newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ALPINE SKIING-GHEDINA WINS DOWNHILL, CRASHES AT FINISH.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-GHEDINA WINS DOWNHILL, CRASHES AT FINISH.

text.p: Italy's Kristian Ghedina kept his concentration just long enough to pip rival Luc Alphand on Saturday and, despite a crash at the finish, collected his third World Cup downhill win of the season and second in succession.

Ghedina roared down the 4.2 kilometre Lauberhorn course, the longest and one of the most demanding on the World Cup circuit, in a course record time of two minutes 24.23, denying Alphand victory by a mere 13/100ths of a second.
Exhausted and jubilant, the 27-year-old Italian then dropped his concentration a fraction too soon after crossing the line and slammed heavily into the safety padding surrounding the finish area.
The force of the impact silenced the large crowd and sent rescue personel and Alpand scurrying to Ghedina's aid.
After a few anxious moments he gingerly got to his feet and waved to the crowd but complained later of a stiff neck.

"I was just so tired I didn't realise what happened, I stopped thinking about the race too soon," Ghedina said after registering his seventh career victory and second at Wengen. "I was so relaxed today, I was singing during inspection. I'm in such good shape now that I know I can do well."
Alphand, still shaken by teammate Adrien Duvillard's serious crash during final training on Friday, was able to blank the incident out of his mind long enough to take second in 2:24.36.

"It way very difficult to concentrate, you're not suppose to think about those things in the start hut," said Alphand, the reigning World Cup downhill champion. "He is my room mate and yesterday I had to pack his things and even though he's OK it was very hard for me because he is my friend."

Fritz Strobl of Austria, the only skier other than Ghedina or Alphand to win a World Cup downhill this season, was third in 2:24.62, just 1/100th of a second ahead of team mate Werner Franz in 2:24.63.
Ghedina, who became the most successful World Cup downhiller in Italian ski history with his win last weekend in Chamonix, began the day level with Alphand at the top of the downhill standings.
But the 27-year-old Italian will now head to next weekend's downhill doubleheader in Kitzbuehel with a slim 20 point advantage on the Frenchman.

"I have 20 points now but we are going to Kitzbuehel and those are Alphand's races," said Ghedina, refering to Alphand's back-to-back wins on the Strief two years ago. "We have a big week ahead of us. My form is great but it will all depend if my legs hold up."
Alphand said: "It's up to Ghedina now to wear the red jersey as the leader of the standings and he'll see how different it is."
Like Friday's training, the race was marred by numerous crashes as several racers struggled on the icy piste.

At one stage it was delayed 30 minutes when American Kyle Rasmussen, a winner on the same course in 1995, went off near the end of his run and was airlifted from the course by helicopter to a hospital in Interlaken with suspected torn knee ligaments.
Other casualties included Liechtenstein's Markus Foser, who broke a finger in a fall, and a course forerunner who was taken off the course on a stretcher with a broken leg.
There was no change in the overall standings. Giant slalom specialist Michael von Gruenigen continues to lead with 577 points, ahead of Norwegian all-rounder Kjetil-Andre Aamodt.
